subject: general
question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 6.**
solution:
The correct answer is: clothes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the meaning and use of the given words. 
 
 
• clothed (**adjective)** means dressed; wearing something
 
• **Clothes ****(noun)** means the things that you wear, for example, trousers, shirts, dresses, coats, etc.
 
• Cloth (noun) means a piece of material that you use for a particular purpose.
 
• **Clothe (****verb**) means to provide clothes for somebody
 
 

 
• So, as per the uses of the given words '**clothes**' is the most appropriate word.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: "**At first a centre for designer dresses**"

​Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

Complete passage: *On Hauz Khas Road, at the entrance to the pedestrianised Hauz Khas Village, the guard (1) at __the barrier asks you to halt and directs __(2) you__ to the parking lot. It's 5 p.m. and the parking lot is nearly empty as shops are closed and there are __(3) hardly__ any shoppers. There aren't many people on the lane leading to the __(4) residential__ area either. This is unusual for HKV (as it is popularly known) __(5) because __it is one of Delhi's popular shopping areas. Initially a hub for designer **__(6) clothes__**, the HKV experience (7)_______ a throbbing mix of cafes, art galleries, curio shops, gyms and, of course, fashion boutiques. The quirky neighbourhood was a hit (8)________ with youngsters and tourists for its happening nightlife. These days however, night comes hours (9)_______ dusk at HKV as you can only see street dogs, security guards, a few takeaway joint managers and bored attendants (10)________ to reach home early.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

 
• **'Cloth' is a singular noun and 'Clothes' is a plural noun.**
 
• **Hub **means the main centre for a specific activity. Therefore, we should not use singular nouns because tonnes of dresses are made there.
